dependencies.basis: BPS implements the 2008 SNA framework (via Supply and Use Tables) for compiling GDP and related national accounts series, including the 2010 base-year rebase.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Since 2010, GDP has been rebased from the year 2000 to 2010 and has implemented the 2008 System of National Accounts (SNA) using the Supply and Use Tables (SUT) as the framework.

dependencies.basis: Provincial GDP (PDRB) is compiled simultaneously with national GDP under the same 2008 SNA framework and 2010 base year to ensure consistency.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Bantuan teknis dan Support ABS terkait Neraca Nasional meliputi kegiatan training dan workshop dalam penyusunan Supply and Use Table (SUT) dan Full Sequence of Accounts (FSA) dalam rangka implementasi SNA 2008 yang ditargetkan akan dirilis perdana pada 2014. ... sebagai benchmark dalam penyusunan PDB/PDRB tahun dasar 2010

dependencies.basis: Bank Indonesia compiles Balance of Payments and International Investment Position statistics according to the concepts, definitions, and classifications of BPM6.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Generally, BOP statistics are compiled based on the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, 6th Edition (BPM6), which includes transactions between residents and non-residents. ... Fundamentally, BOP Statistics are compiled based on the concepts and definitions contained in BPM6.

dependencies.basis: The Indonesia CPI commodity classification follows the international Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP), with recent updates aligned to COICOP 2018.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The international Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) is the commodity classification employed in the Indonesia CPI.

dependencies.basis: CPI compilation methods (including weight updates and index formula) are guided by the CPI Manual concepts and methods.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Based on the CPI Manual (2020), the recommended period for renewing commodity packages is no more than five. The index will be re-based and the weights will be revised according to the 2022 Household Budget Survey (HBS).

dependencies.basis: Susenas household expenditure data serve as an alternative or supporting source for updating CPI expenditure weights and consumption patterns (alongside the primary HBS).
dependencies.evidence_quote: In Statistics Indonesia, one of the alternative data sources that portrays household expenditure is National Socio-Economic Survey (SUSENAS). ... The grouping of goods and services captured in the consumption module Susenas is also guided by the 2018 COICOP, the same as was done for the HBS and CPS. Therefore, this data can be used as an alternative approach to annual CPI reweighting.

dependencies.basis: Household final consumption expenditure (PK-RT) estimates in the national accounts are based on per-capita consumption expenditure data from Susenas, grouped by COICOP divisions.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Estimasi PK-RT untuk harga berlaku didasarkan pada data pengeluaran konsumsi per kapita hasil Survei Sosial Ekonomi Nasional (Susenas). Angka yang dihasilkan kemudian dikelompokkan ke dalam 12 divisi COICOP.

dependencies.basis: CPI detailed breakdowns are used as deflators for household final consumption and other expenditure components in the national accounts.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Detailed breakdowns of the consumer price index (CPI) and producer price index (PPI) are available to use as deflators. ... HFC is deflated with appropriate components of the CPI. So, the implicit deflators are consistent with the CPI, even though they will have different weights.

dependencies.basis: Official poverty incidence and related indicators are calculated from household expenditure data collected in the National Socio-Economic Survey (Susenas).
dependencies.evidence_quote: The data sources used in this publication are data from the March 2022 National Socio-Economic Survey (Susenas).

dependencies.basis: Indonesia Foreign Trade Statistics (Exports) classify commodities according to the Harmonized System (HS) for international comparability, using the Indonesian Customs Tariff Book version of HS.
dependencies.evidence_quote: This publication uses the Harmonized Systems (HS) 2024 classification for international comparability consideration. The data presented here is in units of net weight (kilograms) and FOB value (US dollars) broken down by commodity and country of destination.

dependencies.basis: Indonesia Foreign Trade Statistics (Imports) likewise classify commodities using the Harmonized System (HS).
dependencies.evidence_quote: Indonesia compiles external trade statistics according to the Harmonised Commodity and Coding System (HS). The Harmonised System (HS) is a high-level international nomenclature owned by the World Customs Organisation (WCO), comprising of 6 digits and used by the majority of trading nations.

dependencies.basis: Primary source data for export statistics are the Goods Export Declaration (PEB) documents and related records supplied by the Directorate General of Customs and Excise (customs authorities).
dependencies.evidence_quote: The primary source of export originates from the Directorate General of Customs and Excise in the form of a Goods Export Declaration (PEB) document, PT. Pos Indonesia, border records of other agencies, and exports enumeration in the sea border area.

dependencies.basis: Primary source data for import statistics are customs declaration documents supplied by Customs Authorities under the institutional arrangement with BPS.
dependencies.evidence_quote: There are three sources for external trade data such as the customs declarations provided by Customs Authorities, post dispatch provided by PT Posindo, and cross sea border trade survey. Customs declaration data provided monthly by Customs Authorities based on MOU letter between BPS, Customs Office, and Central Bank.

dependencies.basis: Industries in the national accounts (and SUT) are classified according to ISIC (via the Indonesian KBLI adaptation of ISIC Rev. 4).
dependencies.evidence_quote: International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC), Rev. 4 and the Central Product Classification (CPC) are used to classify industries and products, respectively, with some country specific changes.
